newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs to see flattening post-FOMC - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs to see flattening post-FOMC - dealers.

text.p: The Belgian bond market, buoyed on Wednesday by interest rate optimism reinforced by soft German orders news, will see a fresh batch of flattening trades once the rate hopes are confirmed, dealers said.

Wednesday's volumes were tame, they said, held back in part by foreign hesitancy, not only over the impending U.S. FOMC and Bundesbank rate decisions, but also over Belgian franc weakness due to concerns over domestic political tensions.
News on U.S. interest rates from the FOMC policy makers is due after today's trade has ended in Europe. The Bundesbank's policy-making council meets on Thursday.
The market was expected to pick up the trend towards curve flattening once the rate news was out, dealers said.

The spread between three-month money and 20-year OLOs has already come down to 3.31 percent from 3.46 three weeks ago. Over the same period the three-month/10-year spread narrowed to 2.71 percent from 2.87.

"Belgian investors remain buyers on dips," said a trader. Another confirmed there was buying interest, but also noted this might shift to Bunds once the political tensions abated and the franc recovered. It was at 20.6315 to the mark at 1235 GMT compared with 20.6180 three weeks ago before the tensions arose.
"With a weak currency (franc) people are not going to move to the mark, but once it recovers they will," he said.

News German manufacturing orders for December showed a 1.4 percent fall from November's revised 0.5 percent drop lifted OLO futures, but cash prices hardly reacted. Economists had forecast a 3.3 percent rise for December.
Front-month futures were up 40 bps at 122.16 at 1145 GMT.
The market will be looking for confirmation of sluggishness in the German economy from jobless data due later this week.
Bunds and OLOs almost moved in sync. The 10-year OLO/Bund spread was at plus eight basis points, up from Tuesday's seven.

Dealers said uncertainty remained over the political situation in Belgium after arrests, charges and police raids in an alleged bribery scandal, focusing on francophone socialists in the PS, which is in the centre-left coalition.

They noted that the Flemish christian democrats -- the largest coalition partner -- had taken back some of the strong language uttered when the scandal first broke, but added it was unclear how confidence in the PS, and politics in general, would be restored. Concern about corruption deepened this week after raids of 20 offices, some in the Finance Ministry, in connection with a number of cases, some linked to tax fraud.
